data.headline: Senior Product Manager at Microsoft
data.about:
I'm currently working as a Product Manager with the platform security team at Microsoft. I've grown adept at engaging with customers, performing competitive market analysis and helping define the roadmap of the products I work with. The products that I'm working on deal with strengthening the security posture of Windows OS and enabling confidential computing across Azure. I'm also one of the drivers for Microsoft's approach to Zero Trust Networks; I've co-authored a blog on the same here: https://cloudblogs.microsoft.com/microsoftsecure/2018/06/14/building-zero-trust-networks-with-microsoft-365/ 

Formerly, I worked as an Technical Program Manager intern at Facebook where I was responsible for handling and improving processes for the Population Density Program and collaborating with affiliates on the public release of the population datasets of the countries. More information on the same (and the datasets of the countries) here: https://www.ciesin.columbia.edu/data/hrsl/

description.text: As a Product Manager on the Platform Security team, my work deals with the tamper-detection of the Windows operating system. I'm also one of the drivers for Microsoft's Zero Trust Networking approach with M365.
Graduate Teaching Assistant for Online Graduate course CS 6250 (Computer Networks)

I worked as a TPM for the Infrastructure Data Science Team. A few highlights of my contributions: 

• Laid down the technical goals and the roadmap for the Population Density Pipeline program to provide a clear vision and direction to the program.
• Drove the public release of population datasets of countries through an external affiliate and achieved a 60% increase of released countries in 3 weeks.
• Achieved a 100x cost reduction by facilitating a switch of labeling tasks from on-shore to off-shore resources.
• Set up communication channels and task templates in place to facilitate better understanding between the producers and consumers of the data, and between various teams.

• Single-handedly assessed the performance and the functionalities of eNodeB’s in LTE Networks under numerous simulated environments
• Worked closely with the L2 and L3 development teams to identify, isolate and fix critical software issues 
• Developed, integrated and automated various tests using Python and shell scripts; reduced the average validation time duration by over 35%
• Characterized the behavior of eNodeB’s and UE’s in LTE Networks under various load conditions using the IxLoad tool by IXIA

• Collaborated on the development of a data logger designed using SPEAr320EVAL (ARMv5 based) development board; developed the C++ code that captured real-time data and the corresponding timestamp of the packets for the MODBUS-485 and CAN interfaces
• Comprehensively verified the working of CAN, MODBUS-485, RS-232 and GPIO interfaces of the data logger to ensure an accuracy of 1 ms; also documented the existing codebase for better readability

projects.title: Branch Predictor and Cache Performance Evaluation
projects.subtitle: Sep 2016 - Dec 2016

description.text: Associated with Georgia Institute of Technology

• Implemented LRU and NXLRU cache replacement policies for set-associative and fully-associative caches using a C++ based Multiprocessor Architectural Simulator (SESC); also modified the existing simulator code to identify cache misses as coherence, compulsory, capacity and conflict
• Evaluated the cache performance on the basis of metrics such as Cache Hits, Misses and Evictions from cache sets in each core of a multi-core system using the LU Factorization Benchmark 
• Implemented a C++ code for the SESC Simulator to count the number of correct and incorrect mispredictions for every branch instruction in Hybrid and Not-Taken predictors, and compared their performance with the Oracle Predictor.

projects.title: Video Streaming over Software Defined Networks using IP Multicast
projects.subtitle: Sep 2016 - Nov 2016

description.text: Associated with Georgia Institute of Technology

• Implemented IP Multicast for streaming videos using RYU Controller on Mininet, a virtual network emulator
• Developed an application using Python to dynamically assign Multicast IP addresses to the servers from a pool and find the best server for a client based on the shortest path routing algorithm  
• Evaluated the performance of the video over SDN on the basis of QoE metrics such as Pre-Roll Delay, Latency, Throughput, Jitter and Frame Loss for different network topologies using Wireshark

projects.title: Autonomous Navigation Aid for the Visually Impaired (Undergraduate Thesis Project)
projects.subtitle: Jan 2015 - May 2015

description.text: Associated with B. M. S. College of Engineering

• Developed a wearable ultrasonic sensor based system, interfaced with Atmega2560 microcontroller; beta-tested the prototype with the help of visually impaired students
• Developed a time-critical, interrupt-driven code in C that allowed the user to differentiate between static and dynamic obstacles, prioritize obstacles based on proximity and suggest alternate paths for effective navigation
• Was recognized as the best project of the Department; published a research paper on the same
